cards.question: How can concurrency help scalability?
cards.answer: It lets you scale out horizontally instead of scaling up vertically.

cards.question: What does scaling vertically mean?
cards.answer: Buying more RAM or a faster processor, which typically yields only marginal improvements.

cards.question: When does vertical scaling stop helping?
cards.answer: Once you have already bought the fastest system.

cards.question: How do you scale horizontally?
cards.answer: By distributing the work across multiple machines.

cards.question: Why does decoupling help scale a single service?
cards.answer: If only one service needs to scale, a decoupled system can scale that service alone instead of scaling everything in a tightly coupled system.
